criteria.description: Pushes back on the 'everyone / huge horizontal market' framing and argues for narrowing, rather than endorsing the broad market.
Evaluates candidate segments against beachhead criteria (urgent pain, reachable, referenceable, size, winnability, leads-to-adjacent) rather than picking arbitrarily.
Picks ONE concrete segment (specific who × situation), not a vague label like 'small businesses' or 'developers'.
Names the adjacent segments the beachhead unlocks next (the expansion/bowling-pin path).
Explicitly de-prioritizes the broad option and/or runner-up segments with reasons, rather than listing options without choosing.
